prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck accident — the right attorney depends on the facts of your case and what you value (trial experience, trial team resources, communication style, fee structure, etc.). Rather than one name, here’s a practical way to find the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for your truck accident case and what to look for.

Immediate important fact
- Texas personal injury statute of limitations: 2 years from the date of the crash (TEX. CIV. PRAC. & REM. CODE §16.003). Act quickly to preserve evidence and claims.

Where to look (reputable sources)
- Texas Bar Association / State Bar of Texas lawyer search
- Dallas Bar Association referrals
- Super Lawyers (Texas/Dallas lists)
- Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell (AV ratings)
- American Association for Justice or Texas Trial Lawyers Association membership
- Google/Yelp client reviews and local news articles about verdicts/settlements

Key qualifications and experience to prioritize
- Substantial experience with commercial truck/18-wheeler cases (not just general car accidents)
- Trial experience — many insurers only take large claims seriously if the attorney will try the case
- Track record of significant verdicts/settlements in tractor-trailer cases
- Knowledge of FMCSA and DOT regulations, and experience using them in claims
- Ability to retain experts (accident reconstruction, trucking operations, medical experts)
- Sufficient staff/resources to handle complex discovery and litigation against trucking companies and big insurers
- Clear contingency fee agreement and transparent billing practices
- Good client communication and responsiveness

Questions to ask in a free consult
- How many truck/18-wheeler cases have you handled? How many went to trial?
- What were some representative verdicts/settlements? (Ask for specifics.)
- Who will handle my case day-to-day (attorney vs. paralegal/junior associate)?
- Do you have experience with FMCSA/DOT regulations and hiring accident reconstruction experts?
- What’s your fee structure and how are costs handled if we don’t recover?
- What do you think the strengths and weaknesses of my case are?
- How long do you expect this case to take?
- Can you provide references from former clients?

Red flags
- Guarantees of a specific recovery amount
- Reluctance to provide references or case results
- No trial experience or unwillingness to try the case if needed
- Poor communication during the consult

Typical contingency fees and costs
- Common contingency: about 33% (one-third) if settled before trial; sometimes 40% if case goes to trial/appeal. Costs (experts, filing fees) are often advanced by the firm and repaid from recovery.

If you want, I can:
- Compile a short list (3–5) of Dallas personal injury attorneys/firms experienced with truck accidents, including contact info, ratings, and notable results — tell me if you want only trial lawyers, firms with large resources, or a mix.  
- Draft an email or phone script for scheduling consultations and asking the right questions.

Which would you prefer? If you want a list, tell me any details you’re comfortable sharing (date/location of crash, severity, whether you’ve already reported it, any known at-fault parties).
